title: Cross-engine database migration
scenario: Lindqvist Parts Distribution runs its order system on a commercial Oracle database (1.8 TB, about 350 stored procedures written in the database's own procedural language) and a separate 40 GB MySQL 8 database behind its web store, both in its own datacentre. The datacentre lease ends in 7 months and the Oracle licence will not be renewed, so both databases must run in AWS, with the order system on a PostgreSQL-compatible engine and the web store staying on MySQL. Orders arrive around the clock, and copying the 1.8 TB takes about 3 days. Production must never be taken offline for the copy itself.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Order entry may be offline for at most 30 minutes at cutover
Developers will not hand-rewrite the 350 stored procedures from scratch; only what conversion tooling cannot translate may be fixed by hand
Finance caps the period in which the old and new order databases run in parallel at 2 weeks
Operations wants one data-movement service for both databases
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented

The 1.8 TB order database reaches the PostgreSQL-compatible engine with its schema and all 350 stored procedures working there, and order entry is offline for no more than 30 minutes even though the copy takes 3 days
The 40 GB web-store database is prepared with no more work than its situation requires, and the record justifies why the two databases are prepared differently

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
